source.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/08a00.svg, kanji 言 (U+8A00 CJK UNIFIED IDEOGRAPH-8A00), seven stroke paths kvg:08a00-s1 to s7 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
source.variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is the top mark, a dot drawn down to the right (kvg:type ㇔); s2 to s4 are the long bar and the two short bars, each drawn left to right (㇐); s5 is the box's left side drawn top to bottom (㇑); s6 is its top drawn left to right, turning down its right side without lifting (㇕b); s7 is its base, drawn left to right (㇐b). Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. The Japanese print glyph draws the top mark as a short bar, so the path runs along the bar from left to right.

source.variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 to s7 are 言, s8 to s11 五 and s12 to s14 口, each drawn in the same order and directions as KanjiVG's own files for those three, kanji/08a00.svg, 04e94.svg and 053e3.svg. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. As in 言, KanjiVG's first path is a dot drawn down to the right (kvg:type ㇔). The Japanese print glyph draws that mark as a short bar, so the path runs along the bar from left to right.
